title: VPC Endpoints & AWS PrivateLink
summary: Reach AWS services and partner services privately, without internet, NAT or public IPs.
tldr: **Gateway endpoints** exist only for **S3 and DynamoDB**, are free, and work through route table entries. They are the cheapest way to cut NAT gateway charges for S3/DynamoDB traffic.

**Interface endpoints** (PrivateLink) put ENIs with private IPs in your subnets for most other services, cost per hour per AZ plus per GB, and are reachable from on-premises over VPN or Direct Connect.
To publish your own service to many VPCs, even with **overlapping CIDRs**, put it behind an NLB and create a **VPC endpoint service**; consumers create interface endpoints.
Lock down both sides: an **endpoint policy** limits what can be reached through the endpoint, and an `aws:SourceVpce` condition in the bucket or API policy limits who can reach the resource.

keyFacts.text: The only services with gateway endpoints. A gateway endpoint can't be reached from on-premises, a peered VPC or through Transit Gateway; use an interface endpoint there.
With private DNS on, the standard service hostname resolves to the endpoint's private IPs, so SDKs need no code change.
Deny access to a bucket unless `aws:SourceVpce` equals your endpoint ID to force all access through one endpoint.
PrivateLink lets consumers start connections to the provider only; no routing between VPCs, so CIDR overlap doesn't matter.

traps: A gateway endpoint doesn't work for traffic arriving from on-premises; use an interface endpoint for that.
VPC peering or Transit Gateway with overlapping CIDRs fails; PrivateLink is the fix.
ECR image layers are stored in S3, so ECR endpoints alone still send layer downloads through NAT without an S3 gateway endpoint.
Security groups don't apply to gateway endpoints; control them with the endpoint policy.
